text: A data warehouse can span an entire organization. Sometimes a team doesn't need all of that — they need a data mart, a scaled-down slice built for one specific business function.

There are two ways to build one. A DEPENDENT mart is carved out of an existing warehouse — it inherits all that integration work already done. An INDEPENDENT mart is built standalone, loaded straight from source systems, faster to stand up, but without sharing that consistency work.

AdventureWorks D-W twenty fourteen actually has a real example sitting right inside it. It holds two sales channels — internet sales and reseller sales — in separate fact tables. A reseller-operations team querying just Fact Reseller Sales is functionally using a dependent-mart-style slice, without touching internet sales data at all.

Here's why that's worth doing. A full warehouse might span dozens of tables across every subject in the business. A mart trims that down to exactly what one team needs — faster, simpler, and it doesn't compete for resources with every other team's queries hitting the same warehouse.
A warehouse for the whole business, a mart for one corner of it. Next lesson: a completely different storage philosophy — the data lake. See you there.
